newsitem.title: ITALY: Arbiter to assign Bosnian town to Serbs.
newsitem.headline: Arbiter to assign Bosnian town to Serbs.

text.p: An American arbiter has decided that the strategic northern Bosnian town of Brcko will be awarded to Serbs subject to international supervision and guarantees for Moslems and Croats, a senior diplomatic source said on Thursday.

Arbiter Roberts Owen is due to announce his decision in Rome on Friday (1030 GMT) following a meeting with the Contact Group on former Yugoslavia and the international community's High Representative for Bosnia, Carl Bildt.

The source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said he expected the Contact Group, comprising Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Russia, the United States and the European Union presidency, to support the ruling.
"The Owen plan includes requirements on their part, in other words the handing of Brcko to the Bosnian Serbs is conditional on their good behaviour," the source said.

Brcko, which lies on the Sava River, sits on a narrow land corridor which links eastern and western halves of Serb-controlled territory in northern Bosnia and was seized by the Bosnian Serbs early in the 1992-95 war.
The dispute over who should control it almost caused talks which ended the conflict to collapse in November 1995.
The source said Bildt's office would be assigned a supervisory role for the town by Owen, a U.S. lawyer.
Precise details of the supervision requirements were still being ironed out. "The discussion is not so much over the period but whether it should be open-ended or not," the source said.

Owen would require the Serbs to allow Moslem and Croat refugees to return to homes they fled in Brcko during the war and to grant the Moslem-Croat Federation transit rights along the Sava, a trade route to the River Danube.
Arrangements would also be made for an international presence in Brcko's Serb police force, the source added.
Owen heads an arbitration panel on which he is flanked by a Bosnian Serb and a member from the Moslem-Croat federation.

The panel had been due to rule by mid-December but the deadline for settling the dispute was extended until February 15. Serb and Moslem delegations presented their arguments during 10 days of arbitration hearings in Rome last month.
Moslem leaders have said Brcko should be awarded to the federation based on the pre-war population in which Moslems and Croats formed a majority.
They argued that giving the port to the Serbs would reward ethnic expulsions carried out when Serb forces captured the area in May 1992.
The Bosnian Serbs have insisted that the town must be kept under Serb control or Serb territory would be cut in half and had threatened to go to war over the issue.
